coverage.statement: 1,592 of the 4,776 people in the gallery have no usable reference face (1,430 have no Commons reference at all): for them verify can only answer 'no usable reference'. That is a ceiling on coverage, apart from the threshold. In calibration, a name that resolves only to such a person is unscorable, as is one that resolves to several people (verify refuses it): it counts as a rejection against TAR (cost_in_true_accepts; tar_scorable leaves it out), as coverage when a person confirms it (review_findings), and never as a true or a false accept.

population.what: Factify2 TRAIN claim images (every record using the image is train) whose claims say an image shows someone and name one figure: exactly one of the probe's listed figures, or else exactly one person by claim NER. The figure is the stratum for per-figure reporting; a name is scored against everyone the image's claims name

vlm_precision.rule: right when the name resolves, by QID, to anyone the image's claims name: the probe's listed figures and claim NER's people. A claim name that resolves to several people decides nothing
vlm_precision.note: The earlier figures carried a defect in this measurement: the pilot's 47.8% and the first QID-based figure (0.5455, the 2026-10-21 sample pass) scored a name against one figure per image, so a person the claims name beside that figure, correctly named, counted as wrong. Both were understated. single_figure_rule is that defective figure recomputed on these trials. The token rule is the pilot's own method on the same images: its loose token pattern, with the same defect. The pilot's 47.8% is also APPROXIMATE for that token pattern

threshold.chosen_by: unset: no threshold reaches the one-sided 95% lower bound of 0.90, and a point estimate is never adopted, so the gallery does not decide at this confidence. Short of the bound: the highest lower bound of accepted-name precision is 0.8658, at 0.5214: 129 of 141 accepted names right (0.9149). That clears 0.90 as a point estimate, on too few trials to certify it: at that precision about 1,183 accepted names would
threshold.candidate_by: closest to the bound and short of it: the highest lower bound of accepted-name precision is 0.8658, at 0.5214: 129 of 141 accepted names right (0.9149). That clears 0.90 as a point estimate, on too few trials to certify it: at that precision about 1,183 accepted names would

bound_shortfall.statement: the highest lower bound of accepted-name precision is 0.8658, at 0.5214: 129 of 141 accepted names right (0.9149). That clears 0.90 as a point estimate, on too few trials to certify it: at that precision about 1,183 accepted names would

cost_in_true_accepts.note: TAR is (right names the gallery can score / right names) x tar_scorable: a name it cannot score is coverage, and tar_scorable is the recognizer's own rate without it

figures.what: per figure, the image's stratum, most trials first: trials and what the candidate threshold accepts of them. Local report only: the published one gives ranks, never a name or QID

concentration.statement: The two most-tried figures carry 48% of the trials; the figure-stratified estimate weighs every figure the same, beside the pooled one.

figure_stratified.what: every figure weighs the same: each trial counts 1 / its figure's trials; 95% intervals by resampling figures
figure_stratified.note: the threshold at which the one-sided 95% lower bound of figure-weighted precision reaches 0.90; when it is above the pooled one, the pooled threshold leans on the most-tried figures

look_alike_finding.what: the VLM's wrong names against random strangers: the right names' faces, each scored against a random other person in the gallery, over 200 seeded draws (the first is the one reported field by field). A contrast, never an input

if_calibrated_on_random_pairs.rule: the lowest threshold at which p*TAR / (p*TAR + (1-p)*FMR) >= 0.90 with FMR measured on random strangers (point estimate), p the VLM's QID precision

look_alike_finding.finding: Calibrated on random pairs, the threshold would sit at 0.242 (0.216 to 0.269 over 200 draws of strangers) and give the VLM's own names an accepted-name precision of 0.754 (0.728 to 0.767), against the 0.9 required: 0 of the 200 draws reach it. 30 of the 70 scorable wrong names score above the 99th percentile of 28,890 stranger scores (0.354); a wrong name outscores a random stranger with probability 0.8693, and a right name a wrong one with probability 0.8494. The count of wrong names above every stranger is one draw's maximum, and it ran from 9 to 37 over the draws: not a statistic, so not used. A random-pair false-match rate measures strangers; the names a gallery must refuse are the look-alikes the VLM chose, so the threshold is calibrated on those.

above_every_stranger.not_used: one draw's maximum: it moves with the draw

sface.verite: not read: calibration reads Factify2 train only

factify2_ledger.note: the full calibration needs the finished run; a partial ledger gives a partial population and never sets the threshold

alias_gaps.what: the build scope's PERSON names as resolution sees them (the name table, mentions in scope), and plausible aliases that do not collapse: rules for counting, never links. Names of two words or more that resolve to no one: spacing, initials_or_middle, spelling (name_variant) against gallery people's labels and aliases. One word: the same letters as one person's spaced name, or the person holding 90% of 10+ mentions of our full names with that surname (first name, for a word never used as a surname)
alias_gaps.statement: Of 12,627 person names, 4,837 resolve to one person; 850 of them collapse into the 374 people who have two names or more. 344 names (2,240 of 58,032 mentions) plausibly name a gallery person they do not resolve to: 232 resolve to no one, 112 to several people and 0 to someone else

labels.statement: Of the 104 trials the label rule does not call right, an alias gap may decide 2; a claim's text carries the name of 13 (a handle, or a name NER did not find), which the review sheet shows a person

resolution_rules.what: over the build scope's person names, what each resolver rule changes against an exact key: spacing looks a name up by its letters, as linking does; one_word lets a one-word name resolve only to the one gallery person who holds it, never through a nickname alias, and makes a word with two readings or more ambiguous

cost_by_design.statement: 459 names that resolved to one person (4,229 mentions, 7.3% of all) now refuse rather than guess: the word is several people's, or only a nickname. A design choice, not a regression: a guess checks one person's face, and nothing downstream can tell a wrong guess from a right one

resolution_rules.statement: 459 names that resolved to one person (4,229 mentions, 7.3% of all) now refuse rather than guess: the word is several people's, or only a nickname. A design choice, not a regression: a guess checks one person's face, and nothing downstream can tell a wrong guess from a right one. Against an exact key, the rules change how 765 names resolve (5,259 mentions): spacing 42, one_word 725

no_one.what: the build scope's person names that resolve to no one, by the first cause that applies: an alias gap; a one-word name the resolver refuses; what Wikidata's search answered at linking
no_one.statement: 7,075 person names (11,447 of 58,032 mentions) resolve to no one. Exact matches held for a person's check: 637 (721 mentions). Linking failures with the person in the gallery, by rule: 219 (705 mentions). One-word names the resolver refuses: 44 (474 mentions). No Wikidata item by that name: 4,337 (5,880 mentions), and items that begin with it but are not it: 540 (853 mentions) -- people Wikidata does not have, or forms its search cannot match. Exactly a name item, a surname or first name alone: 105 (178 mentions); exactly something that is no person: 883 (1,985 mentions); both: 310 (651 mentions)

adjudicated.by: a person, by eye, on the review sheet
adjudicated.note: a trial without a decision keeps its label; relabelled says how many decisions changed a label, and in which direction, and how many confirmed it

review_findings.what: every name a person decided, by where the gallery puts it against its consistency threshold: a confirmed name below it is a recognition failure, one it cannot score is coverage; label noise (decisions that changed a label) is counted apart

rules.pose: side-on: the nose 0.5 eye spans or more from the eyes' midpoint, along the eye line -- past the far eye
rules.size: eyes to mouth, smaller than every face the gallery recognised among the confirmed names (the smallest: 20.0 px)
rules.occlusion: the mouth region's skin share 0.6 or more below the eyes' band, on the aligned crop: a mask over nose and mouth

remedies.pose: references in more poses, a side view for a side view
remedies.size: none in the gallery: under the 20 px floor verify answers no_usable_face, and only a larger image helps
remedies.occlusion: none in the gallery: the recognizer scores what the mask leaves

review_findings.statement: A person confirmed 148 names right. The gallery scores 146 at or above its floor of 0.381; 0 below it, among different people's faces -- recognition failures, not label errors: they lower TAR, and they are the recognizer's limit on these images (pose: 0, size: 0, occlusion: 0, more than one: 0, neither: 0); 2 it cannot score -- coverage, never a true accept. 14 decisions changed a label (label noise): wrong to right: 14 (14 at or above the floor, 0 below it, 0 unscorable)
